newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish fx bonds to trade on Istanbul Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Turkish fx bonds to trade on Istanbul Exchange.

text.p: Foreign currency-denominated bonds introduced by the Turkish Treasury two weeks ago began trading on the Istanbul Stock Exchange's repurchase and reverse repurchase market on Thursday, the Exchange said.
Banks and brokerage houses will be able to sell or buy the total $1.12 billion worth of three-year dollar-denominated bonds in dollar terms by making repo or reverse repo deals.
Trading between banks and brokerages outside the bourse is not allowed, but they can trade the forex-denominated bonds with their customers or the central bank.
Besides trade, the new bonds can also be used for liquidity requirments and as collateral.

The bonds, planned as part of the government's first revenue-raising package unveiled on July 31 to fight huge deficits, were bought by the banks with an interest rate of LIBOR plus 260 basis points on Wednesday.
The Treasury had asked banks two weeks ago to submit their bids for the bonds which have a put option at the end of the second year.
The government aims to extend the maturities and relieve the burden of heavy domestic borrowing in Turkish lira. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
